thread:
Alex W: Quick sync — PM asks we prioritize the PRD for private deployments (VPC/on‑prem) v2. Main asks from customer: static egress IP + KMS integration + faster onboarding hooks. Need a PRD draft + acceptance criteria by EOD Friday. Who can take RFC lead?

Priya Nair: I can own the PRD draft. Can someone fetch the latest acceptance criteria from the ops checklist so I can reuse it?

Ben Kline: Pasting key takeaways verbally for now: BGP/egress IP handoff, NAT option, KMS key rotation, control plane auth, log/metrics forwarding, test harness for egress validation. Will add detail into the doc.

Samira Chen: Add an edge case — customers with overlapping CIDR ranges. We need a fallback: NAT translation recommendation or documented requirement for nonoverlap.

Carla (customer): FYI — our infra team needs per-tenant NAT and guaranteed static egress IPs. We can provide a staging cluster next week for testing.

InfraBot: Note: PRD template updated 2026-03-10 — /docs/prd_template.md

Alex W: Baseline acceptance criteria (sketch):
```
- Deployment validated in customer staging across 2 AZs
- Networking: customer-controlled egress available via documented BGP peering OR NAT (config guide included)
- Security: KMS-managed keys + key rotation tested; audit logs enabled and exported to customer SIEM
- Observability: token-level tracing + 99th percentile downstream latency < 300ms at 1k qps baseline
- Rollout: canary with 10% initial traffic, automatic fallback on error thresholds
- Upgrade path: zero-downtime model/version pinning supported for private control plane
```

Priya Nair: Thanks. Ben — can you enumerate concrete tests for each bullet so I can convert them to tickets?

Ben Kline: Short test matrix entries: BGP peering handshake + route advertisement check, NAT egress verification script (assert external IPs), TLS cert rotation exercise, KMS key rotation & access audit, egress IP validation harness, log forwarder end‑to‑end smoke. I'll upload a spreadsheet.

Samira Chen: Another edge-case: some customers sit behind strict outbound proxies allowing only TLS1.2. Verify our runtime and sidecars support TLS1.2 negotiation and proxy CONNECT behavior.

Alex W: Prioritization thought: customer-driven asks (static egress + KMS) = P0 for this quarter. Everything else P1. Agree? @Priya Nair @Ben Kline

Priya Nair: Agree. I'll structure PRD into scope (P0/P1), acceptance criteria, rollout plan, test matrix, and open questions.

Carla (customer): For rollout, we strongly prefer phased DNS cutover (we run DNS) rather than provider-side IP rewrites. We'll coordinate change windows.

Ben Kline: Noted — DNS switch approach is fine but will add e2e test cases for TTL and rollback. I will also draft a minimal test harness for egress IP verification customers can run.

Alex W: Plan: Priya to post PRD link by tomorrow 10:00am PT, Ben to attach test matrix, Samira to write up network edge cases (CIDR overlap, proxy constraints). Reconvene Thurs 14:00 PT for RFC review. If you can't make it, leave comments in the doc.

Priya Nair: On it — will include a short 'open questions' section for gating items (customer cert provisioning, KMS network access, minimum AZ requirement).

Samira Chen: Added initial network edge-case list to the draft and flagged an IPv6 handling question.

Alex W: Great — thanks everyone. I'll follow up with schedule invite and link when PRD is live. :thumbsup:
